A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SMDS research, despite the changed title and formatting. All 25 pages of v1 and 37 pages of v2, including Appendices A–D, provide readable text, equations, tables and figures supporting comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original manifold-fitting results, temporal and geographic task accuracies, noise interventions, randomized-label controls and comparisons across language models.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds repeated-validation statistics, bootstrap comparisons, dimensionality sensitivity results and dataset variability measurements.

M1.justification: The SMDS distance-based objective, MDS construction, regularized linear projection, candidate geometries and default dimensionality remain unchanged. Appendix C already documented the fitting procedure in v1; v2's expanded explanation and statistical validation do not establish a changed projection algorithm.

E1.justification: The eight temporal tasks and geographic reasoning task remain. Appendix B.1 newly evaluates prior numeric-property and weekday/month datasets for variability. The stated US/Canada city eligibility also broadens from populations above 100,000 to above 10,000, although the PDFs do not establish that the geographic experiments were rerun.

E2.justification: v2 adds a randomized-label SMDS comparator specifically to the two-dimensional duration experiment (Table 4); v1's corresponding experiment lacked this comparison. The PCA/LDA/PLS illustration and random-subspace/full-space intervention comparators remain.

E3.justification: The principal validation changes from five-fold cross-validation to ten-fold validation, and a separate bootstrap protocol trains on resampled data and evaluates out-of-bag samples. Added analyses vary dimensionality over {2,3,4,5,10} and measure BERTScore F1 over 5,000 sampled text pairs. These substantially extend the evaluation design.

E4.justification: Appendix D.4 supplies a dimensionality sensitivity study where v1 only stated that higher dimensionalities gave similar results. Appendix B.1 adds dataset variability analysis, and Section 5.4 adds controlled evidence for the two-dimensional manifold. Section 5.3 also newly reports weaker effects from interventions at later layers.

E5.justification: Beyond v1's five-fold averages, error bars and correlation tests, v2 reports ten-fold validation repeated five times, 500 bootstrap iterations, Friedman/Nemenyi rank tests and Wilcoxon comparisons for the two-dimensional control. Tables 3, 4 and 9 report standard errors, and intervention figures newly display and identify standard-error bands.

E6.justification: v2 Table 3 replaces v1 Tables 5 and 8 with revised validation scores and some changed rankings: base Llama-3.2-3B's duration result changes from linear/euclidean at 1.899 to log_linear at 2.879. These use different validation protocols and are not same-setting gains. v2 also adds bootstrap, variability, sensitivity and controlled two-dimensional results, and revises intervention curves.

T1.justification: Appendix D.4 adds the general geometric bound that m dimensions accommodate at most m+1 mutually equidistant cluster centers, supporting the dimensionality discussion. The SMDS derivation, stress definition and geographic distance formulas are retained; no substantial new proof framework is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion narrow the headline methodological claim from automatic manifold discovery to evaluating supplied geometric hypotheses, making explicit a restriction already implicit in v1's model-selection formulation. The three principal empirical claims about shared geometry, contextual adaptation and reasoning remain.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly discusses dependence on the quality and breadth of candidate geometries and the need for suitable labels. It newly acknowledges that logarithmically spaced synthetic labels could explain apparent temporal compression, and proposes contextual reconstruction as an explanation for weaker later-layer interventions. These materially qualify applicability and interpretation.

D1.justification: Section 4 newly specifies that manifold visualizations use the best-scoring layer and a 50/50 train/test split. Figure 21 clarifies that the geographic visualization uses the flat hypothesis. The code-access pointer changes from arxiv2025-shape-happens to tmlr2026-manifold-analysis; the PDFs do not establish changes to repository contents.

R1.justification: Appendix A substantially expands the probing literature, covering linguistic and structural probes, sparsity, truthfulness and the distinction between decodability and mechanistic use. It also adds topology-preserving methods and newer SAE research. Sections 2 and 6 explicitly position SMDS as complementary to existing dimensionality-reduction methods.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, headings and several explanatory passages adopt hypothesis-driven analysis terminology. v2 adds a contents page and reorganizes supplementary material into additional subsections. The main section order, F1–F3 narrative and much of the original prose remain.

P2.justification: v2 switches from two-column to single-column journal formatting, redraws the overview figure and adds rank-comparison and sensitivity plots. It consolidates the original model-result tables, moves geographic results and the two-dimensional visualization into the main text, and adds uncertainty bands to intervention plots.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens a central weakness of v1: selecting preferred geometries from closely clustered scores. Repeated validation, bootstrap rank comparisons and the controlled two-dimensional experiment provide more assessable evidence, while the hypothesis-dependent scope and synthetic-label confound are stated more clearly. Reporting remains imperfect: Section 5.1's universal best-hypothesis wording conflicts with Appendix D.3's date_temperature exception. Nevertheless, the added validation and clearer limitations constitute a substantial net improvement.
